title: Absolute singular ideals under regular ring maps
statement: Let $f:R\to S$ be a regular homomorphism [def-weil-pbc-g-ring] of commutative Noetherian rings [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring]. For either ring $A$, define $\operatorname{Sing}(A)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:A_{\mathfrak p}\text{ is not regular local}\}$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum, def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime, def-weil-regular-scheme] and $s(A)=\bigcap_{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Sing}(A)}\mathfrak p$, with empty intersection $A$. Assume $\operatorname{Sing}(R)$ is Zariski closed. Then for every prime $\mathfrak q\subset S$, $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local if and only if $R_{f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)}$ is regular local. In particular $\operatorname{Sing}(S)$ is closed and is the inverse image of $\operatorname{Sing}(R)$ under contraction of primes. The extended ideal $s(R)S$, generated by $f(s(R))$, is radical and equals $s(S)$; radical means that $x^n\in s(R)S$, $n\ge1$, implies $x\in s(R)S$. No finite-type, excellence, localness or faithful-flatness assumption on $f$ is imposed.

source.place: Tag 07QK, lemma-reduced-goes-up, applied after quotient base change to R/s(R); combined with the regular local-ring ascent/descent criteria. This is the generic ideal-theoretic comparison in Rotthaus (1979), Corollary 4.2(A), proof of Theorem 3, Claims 1–2, pp.176–177 (read online; archival copy WANTED in report).

proof.text: Fix $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Spec}S$ and put $\mathfrak p=f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. By regularity locality, $g:R_{\mathfrak p}\to S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular. Both rings are Noetherian by localization Noetherianity. The fraction formula $r/t\mapsto f(r)/f(t)$ shows that $g$ is local: an element with numerator outside $\mathfrak p$ maps to a unit, and a numerator in $\mathfrak p$ maps into $\mathfrak qS_{\mathfrak q}$. By the definition of regular map, $g$ is flat and its closed fibre is geometrically regular. Taking the trivial finite purely inseparable extension of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ in that definition gives regularity of the closed fibre $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pR_{\mathfrak p}S_{\mathfrak q}$; the fibre/quotient identification is part of the fibre-ring definition.

If $R_{\mathfrak p}$ is regular local, apply flat local ascent with the regular closed fibre from Step 1 to conclude that $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local. Conversely, if $S_{\mathfrak q}$ is regular local, apply flat local descent to the same local map $g$. Both applications have Noetherian local source and target and flatness from Step 1. Negating the equivalence, $\mathfrak q\in\operatorname{Sing}(S)$ if and only if $f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)\in\operatorname{Sing}(R)$.

Put $I=s(R)$. It is radical: if $x^n\in I$, then $x^n$ belongs to each singular prime, and primality, iterated $n$ times, gives $x$ in each such prime. Since $\operatorname{Sing}(R)$ is closed, write it as $V(J)$ for an ideal $J$. The radical/intersection theorem gives $I=\sqrt J$, hence $V(I)=V(J)=\operatorname{Sing}(R)$. For every prime $\mathfrak q$ of $S$, the definition of the generated ideal gives $IS\subseteq\mathfrak q$ if and only if $f(I)\subseteq\mathfrak q$, equivalently $I\subseteq f^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$. Step 2 therefore yields $\operatorname{Sing}(S)=V(IS)$, proving both inverse-image equality and closedness.

The rings $R/I$ and $S/IS$ are Noetherian: for any ideal in either quotient, take its inverse image in the original Noetherian ring and project a finite generating set back down. Also $R/I$ is reduced, since $(x+I)^n=0$ implies $x^n\in I$, hence $x\in I$ by Step 3. The quotient map $R\to R/I$ is finite type (the image of $R$ already generates it as an $R$-algebra). Thus regular base change gives a regular map $R/I\to S\otimes_R(R/I)$. The tensor-quotient isomorphism identifies its target with $S/IS$, compatibly with $R/I$ by the displayed pure-tensor formulas in that theorem. Apply reducedness ascent for regular maps to these two Noetherian rings. Hence $S/IS$ is reduced. If $y^n\in IS$ then $(y+IS)^n=0$ in this reduced quotient, so $y\in IS$. This proves that $IS$ is radical.

source.place: Tags 07C1 (lemma-regular-base-change) and 07QK (lemma-reduced-goes-up); tensor quotient identification: Algebra, Tag 00DF

proof.text: By Step 3 the singular primes of $S$ are precisely those containing $IS$. The radical/intersection theorem now gives $s(S)=\bigcap_{\mathfrak q\in V(IS)}\mathfrak q=\sqrt{IS}=IS=s(R)S$, the penultimate equality being Step 4. All intersections allow the empty family: if the singular locus of $R$ is empty, $I=R$ and $IS=S$; if $S$ is the zero ring, it has no primes and both sides are its unit ideal. No step requires $\operatorname{Spec}S\to\operatorname{Spec}R$ surjective; local descent was applied only at primes actually present in $S$.

The delivery is one commit with no new nodes, and the item statement is unchanged and true. Step 1: 07C0 (lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-maximal) makes R_p→S_q regular. It is local by the fraction formula, and both rings are Noetherian by 00FN. Taking k'=k in the regular-map definition gives a regular closed fibre S_q/pS_q. Step 2: 031E ascent and 00OF local descent; each has all its hypotheses (local, Noetherian, flat, regular fibre). Step 3 (elementary, 00E0 node): I=s(R)=√J, so Sing(S)=V(IS); the closedness hypothesis is used here. Step 4: R→R/I is of finite type, so 07C1 applies (checked more-algebra.tex l.10413). 00DF identifies S⊗R/I with S/IS. R/I is reduced, and 07QK (l.10533) gives S/IS reduced, so IS is radical. Step 5 (elementary): s(S)=√(IS)=IS. Edge cases checked: S the zero ring, Sing(R) empty (I=R), identity, localization maps that are not surjective on Spec. The descent is local only, so no faithful flatness is needed. Searched for duplicates (07QK, regular map with radical, singular locus); every hit is in the parent patching chain and none states this general ring-map comparison.
